correctness.rationale: Fixing r edges gives the claimed all-one moments by counting matchings on the remaining vertices. For an exchangeable extension the difference of the (m-1)- and m-coordinate all-one moments is the expectation of a nonnegative hypergeometric term, zero only at T<=m-2 or T=N. With p_N=q this leaves a triangular system, with p_{m-3}=2q binom(N,m-3)(m+4-N), proving the sharp necessary bound and uniqueness. At N=m+4 the proposed generating polynomial plus q z^N reproduces all binomial moments, including normalization. Coefficient comparison in the formal differential identity and subtraction of the alternating constant transform yield the stated recurrence; the even lower bound b_k=k(k-1)(k+1)/3 supplies 2(k-1)b_{k-1}>=2b_k on the following odd step starting at k=5. This proves all coefficients nonnegative, not just those tested. Marginalization supplies all shorter extensions. For m=1 the only law is all ones; for m=2 the first pair must agree, so exchangeability makes all coordinates agree in any finite or infinite extension. The independent exact replay checked the recurrence through k=100, extremal moments for 3<=m<=35, 165 admissible (m,N) pairs and direct matching moments through m=6; at m=3 the extremal masses are 14/15 and 1/15 at T=1,7.
residual_risks: The proof concerns the complete graph and a uniform matching with a designated perfect matching. The finite replay does not independently establish the all-m recurrence induction.
